subject: Clarify: token rounding on long-context sessions + exception process
messages:
From: Acme Corp DevOps <devops@acme-corp.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify rounding for very long context sessions

Hi Soojin,

We're reconciling May usage and noticed a handful of very long-generation sessions (30k+ input tokens, ~5–10k generated) where the invoice shows rounding up to the next 1k token bucket for every sub-call. That blows up our unit counts.

Can you confirm how Redwood rounds for streaming sessions that splice into multiple inference calls (prefix caching + refill calls)? Specifically:
- Is each server-side call charged independently with its own rounding increment?
- Do KV-cache hits reduce billed input tokens on subsequent calls?

Attached is a small usage snippet (usage_snippet-202705.csv) showing three sessions from our staging app. If there's a known way to flatten those into a single-billing-window or apply a per-session minimum waiver, we'd like to understand it — we're evaluating a bigger commitment but this variance matters for our forecast.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Martinez
Director, AI Platforms | Acme Corp

--
Attachment: usage_snippet-202705.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify rounding for very long context sessions

Alex — thanks for the snippet, that's helpful. Short answer: under our current metering policy each inference RPC is meter-aggregated into a rolling billing window, but rounding is applied at the metering-event level before aggregation in some code paths. That can lead to over-counting in the "many small RPCs composing one logical session" pattern.

I'll summarize:
- Streaming/partial-fill calls: metering records each RPC's token usage. There is a rounding quantum (1 token normally, but in some legacy paths we round up to 100 tokens for performance reasons).
- Aggregation: we attempt to stitch consecutive RPCs with matching session ids into a single billing group for the invoice generation pass, but if calls land on different worker processes without shared session metadata they may be treated separately.
- KV reuse: cached KV doesn't reduce the original input token count for that RPC, but we credit repeated prefix tokens in later RPCs only when the session id is preserved across the RPC boundary.

I don't want to hand-wave here — looping in Ben from finance and Vanessa from CS to propose a concrete exception path for accounts like Acme that hit this pattern. Ben, Vanessa: can you review the attached sample and advise on a pragmatic concession (credit or one-off smoothing) while we push an engineering fix?

Proposed next steps:
1) Redwood performs a one-time smoothing on May for sessions matching the pattern (we can automate detection).
2) We offer a one-time credit equivalent to the delta (or convert to a healthy discount on their next month).
3) Engineering scopes a fix to ensure per-session stitching by June patch release.

Alex — are you ok if we surface the sample to the billing team and run the detection across your account? We will treat this as sensitive.

Thanks,
Soojin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: acme_sample_invoice.csv (CSV, 8KB)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, alex.martinez@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify rounding for very long context sessions

Soojin / Alex — quick finance perspective. We can do a one-off smoothing credit but need a defensible, repeatable rule to apply so it doesn't become a manual playbook that scales poorly. Proposed rule:

- Eligibility: sessions where total logical input+output tokens > 20,000 AND at least two RPCs with the same logical session id that were billed as separate events.
- Calculation: compute the difference between the sum of rounded per-RPC billed tokens and the rounded total of the stitched session; credit 100% of the delta for the affected billing month.
- Cap: credit capped at 15% of that month's bill or $25k, whichever is smaller.

If engineering can provide a list of session ids for Acme, we can run this retrospective calculation. Vanessa, can CS validate the customer acceptability?

Ben
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: proposed_credit_note.pdf (PDF, 12KB)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@acme-corp.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify rounding for very long context sessions

Alex — thanks for sending the sample. CS is supportive of Ben's rule; it balances operational cost control with protecting the platform from open-ended manual credits. A couple of practical notes for the customer side:

- We'll need a short CSV with session ids and timestamps (our engineering team requested this) — we can work with your DevOps to pull that quickly.
- For the immediate customer ask, we can apply the credit to May and also extend a 10% discount on token bill for June if we find more than 3 affected sessions during the May window to buy time while eng ships a patch.

Alex: are you able to provide the session-id list or grant a read-only query to our billing-facing tool? If not, we can scope a small data export job (estimated 2–3 engineer hours).

Happy to coordinate a 30-minute call if helpful.

Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@acme-corp.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify rounding for very long context sessions

Thanks, all — appreciate the quick triage and concrete rule. We're happy to provide the session-id list; I'll ask DevOps to drop the CSV into the shared S3 folder and ping you with the link. Two quick asks:

1) Please confirm the cap language (15% / $25k) — we may ask for a higher cap if our June pilot expands but for now that seems fair.
2) Can the proposed 10% June discount be applied as an invoice-level credit rather than an account-level perpetual adjustment? We prefer an invoice-credit line.

If both are OK, let's run the retrospective and accept the credit for May while engineering patches the stitching behavior. Also happy to join a 30-minute sync tomorrow morning PT.

Alex
